evidence.exact_quote: `Plans/Release_Supply_Chain.md` owns Puppet Master release/install/update provenance, release migration and rollback gates, binary/hash/signing/SBOM expectations, AI-assisted CI taint protections, release tag/currentness policy, and release-facing supply-chain receipts. It does not own provider behavior, credential storage, file safety, GitHub transport, or GUI presentation; those remain with their named owner docs and consume this release/supply-chain contract.

items.impact: The release document has an explicit owner boundary and names adjacent domains that must consume rather than duplicate its contracts.
items.statement: Release, install, update, migration, rollback, provenance, currentness, and AI-CI taint contracts are owned here, while provider, credential, file-safety, GitHub-transport, and GUI presentation behavior remains delegated to named owner documents.
items.title: Release supply-chain ownership is explicitly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Major version migration has backup/restore test.

items.impact: A major update cannot satisfy the PlanUnit without exercising backup restoration, link validation, protocol mismatch blocking, and terminal-session preservation.
items.statement: RSC-001 makes backup/restore testing a release gate and pairs it with generated-link, protocol-mismatch, and session-preservation acceptance checks.
items.title: Major migration has a concrete backup and restore gate

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: 'Need a release compatibility plan: canary/stable rings, artifact provenance, generated-link checks, state migration tests, downgrade/backup restore, extension/CLI/server protocol handshake, terminal session preservation across updates.'

items.impact: Builders could implement incompatible notions of preflight, commit, cancellation, restart, downgrade, partial migration, restore, and concurrent update safety while still passing the four listed acceptance bullets.
items.statement: RSC-001 names canary/stable rings, migration, downgrade, restore, protocol handshakes, and session preservation but does not define their state machine, atomicity boundary, cancellation rule, retry/idempotency behavior, concurrent-update exclusion, backup validity/retention, or fail-safe transition oracles.
items.title: Migration and rollback lifecycle is not defined

evidence.exact_quote: - Release notes/bootstrap docs validate relative links under repo, GitHub rendered, and app routes.

items.impact: Generated documentation has a stated cross-renderer release acceptance surface rather than being checked only as repository text.
items.statement: RSC-002 requires relative links in release notes and bootstrap documentation to validate in repository, GitHub-rendered, and application-route contexts.
items.title: Generated links have a cross-renderer acceptance check

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: Need link-mode validators for generated Markdown across GitHub, local GUI, terminal/plaintext, and app viewer.

items.impact: Terminal/plaintext links, anchors, encoded paths, case sensitivity, route rewriting, offline destinations, inaccessible link labels, and external-link failures can regress without falsifying the current acceptance criterion.
items.statement: The gap text names GitHub, local GUI, terminal/plaintext, and app viewer modes, but the acceptance bullet omits terminal/plaintext and does not define link parsing, anchor, route, offline, external-network, accessibility, localization, or diagnostic-result semantics per mode.
items.title: Link validation modes and failure semantics remain incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: - Every downloadable binary/plugin has SHA256, signing/provenance, build source ref, and install verification.

items.impact: Distributed binaries and plugins must bind integrity, provenance, source identity, and installation verification before release.
items.statement: RSC-003 establishes SHA256, signing/provenance, build-source reference, and install verification as the minimum evidence for every downloadable binary or plugin.
items.title: Downloadable artifacts require integrity and provenance evidence

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: Need release asset signature/hash/SBOM policy for any PM distributed binary/plugin/bridge.

items.impact: A builder can choose incompatible signature formats, trust roots, verification times, revocation behavior, SBOM attachment rules, or omit bridge artifacts because the acceptance criterion narrows the named binary/plugin/bridge scope.
items.statement: RSC-003 does not define accepted signing algorithms and formats, trust-root authority, key rotation/revocation/expiry, verification timing and failure recovery, SBOM identity binding, evidence retention/redaction, or whether bridge artifacts are included in the acceptance oracle.
items.title: Artifact trust lifecycle and bridge coverage are unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Attached server profile cannot be silently mutated

items.impact: Migration tooling is explicitly prevented from silently modifying attached-server state outside Puppet Master's management authority.
items.statement: RSC-004 requires deterministic legacy-name guidance, confines generated bridge configuration to the run working directory or profile root, and prohibits silent mutation of attached server profiles.
items.title: Config migration establishes a non-mutation boundary

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: Add fixtures for accepted current names, retired names with explicit help, JSON/JSONC, generated bridge config cwd/profile root, PM-managed vs attached server config, migration dry-run/rollback.

items.impact: JSON/JSONC ambiguity, mixed old/new keys, malformed input, simultaneous edits, partial writes, repeated migration, dry-run drift, or rollback failure can produce data loss or unauthorized mutation without a deterministic expected result.
items.statement: RSC-004 names current and retired names, JSON/JSONC, management modes, dry-run, and rollback, but its acceptance list does not specify precedence, parser dialect, unknown-key preservation, malformed-input handling, atomic writes, locking, idempotency, backup identity, dry-run equivalence, or rollback-result oracles.
items.title: Config migration fixtures omit critical edge-state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - AI issue/PR triage workflows must default to read-only/no-shell/no-write permissions and require explicit escalation receipts for any tool with filesystem, shell, cache, credential, or release access.

items.impact: Untrusted issue and pull-request text cannot directly gain write, shell, cache, credential, filesystem, or release authority without a receipt-bearing escalation.
items.statement: RSC-005 establishes read-only, no-shell, no-write defaults for agentic issue and pull-request triage and requires explicit escalation receipts before access to sensitive tools or release capabilities.
items.title: Agentic CI starts with least authority

evidence.exact_quote: - All untrusted external text entering an agentic CI prompt carries a taint envelope and cannot be interpreted as tool/policy instructions.

items.impact: Taint can be lost through summaries, tool outputs, caches, artifacts, nested prompts, retries, or human approval, and different implementations can disagree about whether derived content may influence policy or tool execution.
items.statement: The taint requirement does not define an envelope schema, source identity, transitive propagation through derived data and caches, permitted uses, declassification authority, mixed-trust joins, retention/redaction, refusal and recovery states, audit events, or adversarial falsification fixtures.
items.title: AI-CI taint has no executable propagation contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Plans/Release_Supply_Chain.md

items.impact: The taint, escalation, cache, credential, OIDC, publishing, and test requirements can remain release-document prose without an accountable enforcing owner or consuming-call-site contract.
items.statement: RSC-005 lists only the release document as an implementation surface even though its target-doc list names GitHub integration, permissions, decision policy, contracts, automated testing, and governance; it does not assign which owner enforces taint, escalation, cache/OIDC validation, publish denial, or receipt consumption.
items.title: AI-CI enforcement ownership is not propagated

evidence.exact_quote: - Startup diagnostics distinguish code-signing/AMFI/quarantine/GPU/sandbox/network-deny failures from generic launch failures.

items.impact: Platform startup failures must retain actionable class identity rather than collapsing into a generic launch error.
items.statement: RSC-006 requires packaged components to declare platform security and linking state, classifies startup failures, and tests macOS, Windows, and Linux platform-specific conditions.
items.title: Platform launch failures have distinct diagnostic classes

evidence.exact_quote: - Platform matrix CI includes macOS quarantine/signature, Windows sandbox/network, Linux static/dynamic library checks.

items.impact: A nominal three-OS matrix can pass while unsupported architectures or OS versions, dynamic-library floors, sandbox modes, GPU paths, offline behavior, slow startup, inaccessible diagnostics, or nonrecoverable user states remain untested.
items.statement: RSC-006 does not enumerate supported OS versions and architectures, artifact-to-matrix coverage, library and entitlement expectations, diagnostic codes and remediation, recovery/retry behavior, performance thresholds, offline distinctions, accessibility/localization requirements, or the GUI owner's obligation to present the classified state truthfully.
items.title: Platform compatibility matrix lacks coverage and recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Self-update records source/hash/channel/rollback

items.impact: Self-update operations must leave evidence that binds source and hash to an update channel and rollback path.
items.statement: RSC-007 requires install validation to fail on package ownership or mode mismatches, records source/hash/channel/rollback for self-update, and surfaces signing, notarization, and entitlement checks before rollout.
items.title: Install and update flows produce provenance receipts

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: Installer/update flows need artifact signatures, owner/mode inventory, channel, rollback, migration, and validator receipts.

items.impact: Concurrent updaters, interrupted downloads, stale channels, partial installs, lost network, failed migration, invalid rollback targets, or ownership-repair attempts can leave the product in an ambiguous or destructive state while still generating a minimally populated receipt.
items.statement: RSC-007 does not define update states, authorization and process-lock boundaries, download verification order, channel transition rules, rollout pause/cancel behavior, retry/idempotency, partial-install recovery, offline handling, migration coupling, rollback eligibility, or the user-visible truth for each failure state.
items.title: Install and update lifecycle is not specified

evidence.exact_quote: - Install/update validation fails closed when signature, SBOM, artifact hash, migration, or rollback receipt is missing or stale.

items.impact: A release candidate cannot be treated as supply-chain complete when any required signing, SBOM, hash, migration, or rollback evidence is absent or stale.
items.statement: RSC-008 defines minimum ReleaseArtifactReceipt, SBOM receipt, UpdateMetadata, and MigrationReceipt fields and requires install/update validation to fail closed on missing or stale critical evidence.
items.title: Signing, SBOM, update, and migration receipts fail closed

evidence.exact_quote: record channel, version, minimum_supported_version, migration_plan_ref, rollback_ref, and user-visible failure state.
gui_related: false

items.impact: The PlanUnit can be excluded from GUI planning even though it requires a user-visible failure state, leaving failure-state copy, severity, actions, accessibility, localization, and truthful synchronization without an owner.
items.statement: RSC-008 requires user-visible update failure state metadata but classifies itself as not GUI-related and does not bind failure_state_copy_ref to a GUI owner or define presentation, action, accessibility, localization, or stale-state prevention requirements.
items.title: User-visible update failure state conflicts with GUI classification

evidence.exact_quote: - ReleaseArtifactReceipt includes artifact_name, platform, artifact_sha256, size_bytes, signature_ref, key_id, trust_root_ref, notarization_ref?, sbom_ref, and provenance_ref.

items.impact: Implementations can serialize mutually incompatible receipts and disagree on optionality, freshness, verifier authority, key compromise, revocation, artifact/SBOM pairing, migration rollback safety, or evidence retention while claiming the named fields are present.
items.statement: RSC-008 enumerates receipt fields but does not define concrete schemas, identifiers and referential-integrity rules, the meaning of question-mark optionality, freshness windows, trusted clocks, verifier-result enum, accepted algorithms/formats, key rotation/revocation, receipt signing, evidence access/retention/redaction, size and component-count limits, or recovery behavior for stale or partially verified receipts.
items.title: Receipt field lists lack executable semantics and lifecycle rules

segments.summary: Reviewed the prologue and RSC-001 through RSC-004 across migration/rollback, generated-link validation, binary provenance, and config-schema migration. Exact requirements establish meaningful gates and authority boundaries; adversarial review found missing lifecycle, concurrency, trust, renderer-mode, and fixture semantics.

Reviewed RSC-005 through RSC-008 and the release-document addenda across AI-CI taint, platform binary compatibility, install/update provenance, and the signing/SBOM/update/migration minimum. Fail-closed and least-authority requirements are strong; adversarial review found undefined taint and rollout state machines, missing cross-owner bindings, incomplete platform and receipt semantics, and a GUI-classification contradiction.

cross_document_questions: Which named owner document defines and enforces the AI-CI taint envelope, escalation receipt, cache provenance, OIDC provenance, and publish-denial contracts consumed by release workflows?
Which GUI owner consumes update failure_state_copy_ref and platform diagnostic classes, and what contract prevents stale or misleading user-visible release state?
Where are supported OS, architecture, library, entitlement, sandbox, GPU, and network matrix identities canonically enumerated for RSC-006?
Which storage and FileSafe contracts own migration backup identity, retention, encryption, atomic restoration, and destructive-action authorization?
Which artifact/schema owner materializes and validates ReleaseArtifactReceipt, SBOM receipt, UpdateMetadata, and MigrationReceipt referential integrity?
